  "text": "The council replaced our streetlights on a Thursday.

By Friday, everyone’s shadow pointed toward number sixteen.

It had been empty since the fire.

At noon, mine stretched across the road and disappeared beneath its front door.

I phoned the council.

“Are you experiencing flickering?” the woman asked.

“No.”

“Then the installation was successful.”

That night, my shadow stayed on the pavement when I went indoors.

I watched it from the upstairs window. It stood beneath the new lamp, longer than it should have been, with its head tilted toward the burned house.

Around three, it knocked.

Not at my door.

At number sixteen.

Something inside knocked back.

In the morning, my shadow was waiting at my feet.

There was soot on the kitchen tiles.

My neighbour came over carrying a torch.

“Don’t let it know you’ve noticed,” he said.

His shadow raised one finger to its lips.

I looked away.

For six days, I kept every light in the house switched on. I slept beneath a lamp. Whenever I woke, my shadow was where it belonged.

On the seventh morning, the council sent a letter.

FINAL INSPECTION: PLEASE REMAIN HOME AFTER DARK.

I packed a bag before sunset.

At the front door, I felt something pull against my heels.

My shadow had caught hold of the banister.

Outside, the streetlights came on together.

The door of number sixteen opened.

My neighbour stepped out first, carrying his torch. Behind him came the woman from the council, then people I hadn’t seen since the fire.

They crossed the road without casting shadows.

Mine let go of the banister and reached for the lock."
